signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + CB Divergence
signals.text: NZD/JPY has emerged as the G10's dominant bilateral theme, driven by a 2.450% 1W performance spread between the JPY leader and NZD laggard. JPY strength is underpinned by hawkish commentary from the BoJ chief, stating rate hikes remain on the table for every meeting, including this month. This policy pivot contrasts with NZD, which is the weakest G10 performer at -1.433% on average, despite the RBNZ currently hiking. NZD COT positioning sits at an extreme 52-week low (pctl 0, z -2.60), signaling a heavily crowded speculative short that has failed to find a floor. JPY data outperformance (ESI +27.9) further supports the bid against NZD. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; JPY outperformance theme remains structurally dominant. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: NZD short-squeeze on a broad risk-on rally that compresses the 2.450% G10 spread.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Macklem Repricing Risk + COT-OIS Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3842, holding above the SMA20 at 1.3886 and SMA200 at 1.3836 following Bank of Canada Governor Macklem's Tier-1 comments. Macklem warned that markets will reprice if policy fails to achieve inflation objectives, specifically noting a limited tolerance for price growth. This hawkish tilt challenges current speculative positioning, where COT LF net remains short -73,174 (pctl 8, z -1.55). Despite a 150bp carry advantage for the USD, the CAD ESI at +22.8 indicates sustained data beats that may force a further unwind of crowded CAD shorts. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD; policy repricing risk favors CAD strength against crowded shorts. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — hold priced. Risk: USD strength resumes if US yields break higher, overriding the BoC policy shift.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Complacency vs Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY at 158.68 is trading within a bear steepener curve regime, yet the options market exhibits unusual complacency with a negative VRP of -1.7% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.9%). The 25d risk reversal at -1.82 reflects a strong put skew, indicating that while ATM vol is cheap, the market is paying for protection against a sharp JPY move. This skew aligns with the BoJ chief's hawkish stance and the pair holding below the SMA50 resistance at 160.77. JPY COT LF net short of -81,619 remains in the lower decile of its 52-week range (pctl 9), leaving the pair vulnerable to a rapid carry unwind if the 270bp SOFR-TONA spread is challenged by BoJ action. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; cheap optionality and strong put skew suggest a volatility breakout is underpriced. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: US 10Y yields rise toward 5.00%, re-establishing the carry bid and negating the JPY policy bid.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7175 remains supported by a 67bp AONIA-SOFR carry premium and positive domestic GDP data, as noted by BBH. However, speculative positioning has reached a crowded extreme with COT LF net long +53,578 (pctl 95, z +1.92). This institutional long bias is being aggressively faded by retail traders, with 83% of the community currently short AUD/USD. While price holds above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7114/0.7024/0.6978), the institutional vs retail divergence at these extreme levels typically signals late-cycle exhaustion. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; institutional crowding caps further upside potential despite retail fading the trend. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold expected. Risk: A clean break above 0.7250 forces retail capitulation, triggering a secondary momentum leg.
